review.full_review:
Reviewed exact revised plan SHA-256 20b010ce3b37738d69c558e5e2241f592db3262facb5c8a71e0c8eeda6859bb3, its v1-to-v2 changes and all frozen source/input/configuration/validation references. Decision: approve for the stated finite local CPU demonstration, subject to the independent host permissions and later result validation already required by the runtime.

The blocking v1 finding is closed. The producer now contains an explicit prior_result_review selecting a fresh bounded run, acknowledging the missing record in its newly created output namespace, and stating that no prior data are reused. I independently reran the actual prior-result query: it matches the frozen incomplete search, rather than being represented as a successful absence check. The existing producer-disposition validation accepts the recorded rationale. The v1 response and exact old plan remain preserved.

The task remains a concrete three-stage DAG: produce 15 exact-integer samples from five inputs and three repetitions; independently validate code, invalid-input boundaries, sample completeness, closed-form values and aggregate; then write a local scoped summary. Each stage maps to its TASK requirement. The same frozen result contract binds producer, verifier and consumer. Review approval does not mark any future data validated, grant new capabilities, or replace host authorization.

The relative TASK path now resolves against an explicitly trusted host root. The runtime review receipt still binds the actual project identity, so moving the project requires regeneration and a fresh review; this artifact is not an automatic portable deployment promise. No human guide exists in the synthetic project, and no guide write is proposed. Inspected code uses bounded local Python integer work without network, GPU, paid compute, service installation, credentials or external publication.

Acceptance must retain the raw observations and independent post-data checks and report the actual dispatch and consumer outcomes. This finite example can demonstrate the gate transitions and a real independent planning response. It cannot establish model-quality improvement, general correctness, performance gains, measured token savings, or a continuously installed two-model service. Unknown token and cost accounting remain unknown.

verdict.summary: The observed lookup gap is honestly assessed; approve this exact bounded CPU plan with downstream validation and host permissions unchanged.

intent.reason: The three-stage finite CPU task is a proportionate demonstration of protected dispatch and separate result validation. It does not claim model quality or general performance gains.

guide.reason: The synthetic project has no human guide, no adopted advice and no proposed guide writes. TASK requirements map to producer, verifier and consumer.

assumptions.reason: The frozen input integers and exact Python-integer arithmetic support a finite equality test; invalid negative/noninteger/bool input rejection is explicitly checked. General correctness and timing remain out of scope.

prior_results.reason: The current independently rerun lookup exactly matches the frozen incomplete search. The producer explicitly acknowledges the new empty output namespace, chooses a bounded fresh run and claims no reuse or universal absence. The required disposition passes the existing runtime check.

acceptance.reason: The same frozen result contract is bound across producer, independent post-data verification and consumer. The separate verifier checks closed-form values, full sample IDs, aggregate and boundary rejection; plan approval does not validate future data.

risk.reason: Inspected adapter performs bounded local CPU file work, with no network, service, GPU, credentials or external publication. Actual host authorization must remain separate.

resources.reason: Five inputs and three repetitions fit the available local Python CPU. This plan makes no model-token or paid-cost claim; unknown model accounting must remain unknown in any native bridge.

scope: Complete actual review feedback and verdict retained. It approved/revised only its original plan identity, not any redacted view, new plan, current candidate or live host. Host captures are private and are not authenticated by this public view.
